sentences.text: Trial court has failed to appreciate that on dated 02.01.2018, the revisionist no.1/husband of the complainant was in U.S.A. and he came to know that his wife i.e. complainant herein has filed a complaint against namely Sagar Sethi on the allegation that the said Sagar Sethi established physical relations with her forcibly and she was beaten up mercilessly.

On her complaint, FIR No.130/2018 u/s 323/342/376/427/506 IPC PS Mukherjee Nagar was registered and thereafter, it came to the knowledge of the revisionist No.1 in March, 2018 that the complainant herein has settled the case with the said Sagar Sethi and she made the statement before the court that she was in physical relationship with the said Sagar Sethi and also become pregnant with his child.

On her statement,
the said Sagar Sethi was acquitted by the court by passing the detailed judgement.
Thereafter, a divorce petition u/s 13(1)(i) & (ia) of HMA was filed by the revisionist/accused no.1 against the complainant and against two other persons - adultrator no.1 and 2.

It is pertinent to mention that on dated 14.05.2018, the summons of the divorce petition being filed by the revisionist no.1 /accused were served upon the complainant and only after receipt of the summons, a complaint for demand of dowry was made on dated 03.07.2018 addressed to the Assistant Commissioner of Police, CAW Cell, Delhi.

Thereafter, an application u/s 12 Rule 6 of CPC was filed for passing the Judgement on the ground that the complainant has admitted that she was in love with the said Sagar Sethi and the physical relations were established between both of them by her free will and consent.
That, on these grounds, the ld. Judge, Family Court, North vide order dated 03.03.2023 granted decree of divorce to the revisionist no.1 against the complainant u/s 13(1)(i) of HMA.

It is pertinent to mention that perusal of the complaint dated 03.07.2018 made by the complainant against the revisionist to the CAW Cell reveal that there are no specific allegation against any of the revisionists/accused and the said complaint was made only after receipt of the notice of the divorce petition being filed by the revisionist no.1 / accused against the complainant on the ground of adultery which she has admitted and on her admission, a divorce decree on the ground of adultery has been passed.
7.

It is the foremost duty of the court to see that as per the allegations in the FIR and perusal of the chargesheet, any prima facie case is made out only then, the charge can be framed and if there are no specific allegations and are general in nature, then, the court is not bound to frame the charge against the accused persons.

If a person is made to face a criminal trial on some general and speaking allegations without bringing on record any specific instances of criminal conduct, it is nothing but abuse of the process of the court.

The court owes a duty to subject the allegations levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, prima facie, whether there is any gain of truth in the allegations or whether they are made only with the sole object of involving certain individuals in a criminal charge, more particularly, when a prosecution arises from a matrimonial dispute.
Reliance is placed upon ' Achin Gupta Vs. State of Haryana & Ors.' Crl. Appeal No.2379/2024 arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.4912 of 2022.

sentences.text: 8. In another cited case titled as 'Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand' reported in 2010 Crl. Law Journal 4303(1), the court has observed that "It is a matter of common knowledge that unfortunately matrimonial litigation is rapidly increasing in our country.

entities.text: Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand' reported in 2010 Crl. Law Journal 4303(1)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All the courts in our country are flooded with matrimonial cases.
This clearly demonstrates discontent and unrest in the family life of a larger number of people in a society.
The courts are receiving a large number of cases emanating from Section 498A of the Penal Code.
It has also been held by the Hon'ble Apex Court of India that large number of complaints which are not even bonafide and are filed with oblique motive.
At the same time, rapid increase of the number of genuine cases of dowry harassment are also matter of serious concern.

9. It is worth mentioning that before filing the divorce petition by the revisionist no.1 against the respondent, there was not even a single complaint made by the complainant against her husband or his family members for harassment for the demand of dowry and the complaint for harassment and demand for dowry was only made after receipt the copy of the notice of divorce petition being filed by her husband on the ground of adultery.

Therefore, considering all the facts and circumstances,
this court is of the considered view that the impugned order passed by ld.
Trial court is not sustainable inasmuch as there is no specific allegations against any of the revisionist for harassment and for demand of dowry.
The impugned order dated 21.01.2023 is hereby set aside.
The revision petition stands allowed accordingly.
10. TCR, if any, be sent back to the ld.
Trial court with copy of this order

. 
11. File be consigned to record room.
